about.title: Woodside Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Woodside is a small, close-knit community in San Mateo County, and most residents drive into surrounding cities for hospital care, specialist visits, or surgery. When that care goes wrong — a delayed diagnosis, a surgical error, a medication mix-up — the aftermath can be confusing, especially with California's specific rules for these cases. Medical malpractice claims are handled differently than a typical injury case: California's MICRA law sets strict notice periods, expert requirements, and caps on certain damages. We handle medical malpractice claims and understand these rules. We can review what happened at no cost to you. A poor medical result isn't automatically malpractice, but if a provider deviated from accepted medical standards, it's worth having someone knowledgeable look at your records. Contact us so you can find out where you stand.

items.title: Strict, Short Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to file. Missing that window can end a claim before it starts, so timing matters from day one.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before a lawsuit can be filed, California law requires sending the healthcare provider a formal notice at least 90 days in advance. Our team is familiar with this step and can help make sure it's done correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, California cases almost always need a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was breached. We can help get that review process moving early on.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome the same as malpractice?
items.answer: No. Medicine involves risk, and not every complication or disappointing result means a provider was negligent. Malpractice requires showing the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care and that deviation caused harm, which is typically established through expert medical review.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after care received in or near Woodside?
items.answer: California generally requires filing within one year of discovering the injury, and no later than three years from when it occurred, whichever comes first. Because Woodside residents often receive care at hospitals outside the immediate area, it's worth confirming exactly where and when the treatment took place so the timeline is calculated correctly.

items.question: Are there limits on what I can recover in California?
items.answer: California law caps certain non-economic damages, such as compensation for pain and suffering, and that cap adjusts upward each year under current law. Economic damages, like past and future medical costs or lost income, are generally not subject to that same cap.

items.question: Is there a cost for a case review?
items.answer: No. Our case reviews are free. We typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
